advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the space-form flag consuming a following '--'-prefixed token (old behavior) must be preserved; if so, argparse's default nargs diverges and needs handling or an explicit accept-of-divergence note/test.
evidence: Old claim loop: `elif a == "--assignee": ... assignee = args[i + 1]` took the next token unconditionally even when it began with '--'
Old transition loop: `elif a == "--reason": ... reason = args[i + 1]; i += 2` (same unconditional next-token consumption)

New: `parser.add_argument("--assignee", default=None); ns, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args(args)` — argparse default nargs will treat a following '--'-prefixed token as an option, triggering error('argument --assignee: expected one argument')
WriteArgParser.error remaps that to `raise CommandError(f"Error: {m.group(1)} requires a value", returncode=1)` at src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:139-141
advisory.finding: The argparse rewrite changes observable behavior for a space-separated flag whose value itself starts with '--'. The old hand-rolled loop unconditionally took the next argv token as the value (e.g. `_parse_assignee(['--assignee','--review'])` returned '--review'; `_parse_flags(['--reason','--class=x'])` set reason='--class=x'). argparse instead refuses to consume a '--'-prefixed following token as a value and raises 'expected one argument', which WriteArgParser.error remaps to CommandError('Error: <flag> requires a value', exit 1). Same for --class/--caused-by/--ref. This contradicts the commit's stated 'WITHOUT changing observable behavior' invariant.
scenarios: `rebar claim <id> --assignee --review` previously set assignee='--review'; now exits 1 with 'Error: --assignee requires a value'
`ticket transition <id> closed --reason --class=regression` previously set reason='--class=regression'; now exits 1

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting the intended behavior when a space-form flag's value begins with '--' (either preserved as the value, or explicitly documented as a deliberate change).
evidence: The test file pins None-vs-'', value-less exit-1, allow_abbrev, unknown-token skip, and space-separated value with a normal token (`_parse_assignee(['--assignee','alice'])`) but has no case where the following token starts with '--'
ABSENCE: no test asserts the behavior of `_parse_assignee(['--assignee','--review'])` or `_parse_flags(['--reason','--class=x'])`, the exact divergence between the loop and argparse
advisory.finding: The new claim/argparse fidelity test suite does not pin the dash-prefixed-value case (e.g. `_parse_assignee(['--assignee','--review'])`), which is precisely the behavior argparse changes relative to the retired loop, so the regression above would pass CI unnoticed.
scenarios: A future reviewer trusts the 'pins fidelity' claim but the load-bearing divergence is untested

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests asserting _parse_flags(['--reason']), ['--class'], ['--caused-by'], ['--ref'] each raise CommandError with returncode==1 and message 'Error: <flag> requires a value'.
evidence: Rewrite replaces explicit per-flag raises (removed lines: 'raise CommandError("Error: --reason requires a value", returncode=1)', same for --class/--caused-by/--ref) with 'parser.add_argument("--reason", default="")' etc. and 'ns, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args(rest)' at transition.py:153-158
Remap lives in _seam.py: 'm = _re.match(r"argument (\S+): expected one argument", message)' then 'raise CommandError(f"Error: {m.group(1)} requires a value", returncode=1)'
search_files on tests for 'requires a value' returns only tests/unit/test_claim_argparse_parse_fd48.py:40 (--assignee); no transition value-less assertion
tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py exercises _parse_flags extensively but contains no value-less --reason/--class/--caused-by/--ref case (ABSENCE)
advisory.finding: Transition's value-less flag error path (--reason/--class/--caused-by/--ref with no value) is newly routed through the WriteArgParser.error() regex remap, but no test asserts _parse_flags(['--reason']) (or the other three) still raises CommandError with returncode=1 and the historical 'Error: --reason requires a value' message. The old hand-rolled loop raised these explicitly per-flag; the rewrite consolidates them into the argparse remap. The claim test proves the remap only for --assignee, leaving transition's identically-critical path (and the exact-flag-name interpolation in the remapped message) unverified.
scenarios: A regression in the error() regex remap (e.g., argparse message wording change) makes transition emit exit-2 + usage instead of the pinned exit-1 'Error: --reason requires a value'
--class-flag dest remap ('--class' -> close_class) interacts with the reported flag name in the error message
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py (or a transition argparse-fidelity test file mirroring fd48), parametrize over ['--reason','--class','--caused-by','--ref'] asserting _parse_flags([flag]) raises CommandError with returncode==1 and message == f'Error: {flag} requires a value'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no supported input passes a `-`-prefixed value via the space form to --reason/--class/--caused-by/--ref/--assignee, since argparse now rejects such tokens (exit 1) where the old loop consumed them verbatim.
evidence: transition.py:153-158: `parser = write_arg_parser(); parser.add_argument("--reason", default=""); ... ns, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args(rest)`
claim.py:63-66: `parser = write_arg_parser(); parser.add_argument("--assignee", default=None); ns, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args(args)`
Old loop consumed the next token literally: claim.py (pre-change) `elif a == "--assignee": ... assignee = args[i + 1]` with no `startswith('-')` guard — so a `-`-prefixed value was accepted verbatim.

_seam.py:138-142: the `error()` override maps argparse's 'expected one argument' to `Error: <flag> requires a value` (returncode=1), which is what a `-`-prefixed following token now triggers instead of being consumed.

ABSENCE: grep of callsites (tests/integration, tests/interfaces, tests/unit) shows only ordinary non-dash values passed to --assignee/--reason/--class, so no confirmed consumer currently relies on a `-`-prefixed value; divergence is real but low-likelihood.
advisory.finding: argparse-backed value flags (--reason/--class/--caused-by/--ref in transition._parse_flags, --assignee in claim._parse_assignee) narrow the previously-accepted space-separated input: the retired hand-rolled loop consumed the following argv token as the value UNCONDITIONALLY (including tokens beginning with `-`), whereas argparse refuses to consume a `-`-prefixed following token and instead raises `Error: <flag> requires a value` (exit 1). Inputs like `claim <id> --assignee --review` (old: assignee=='--review') or `transition <id> closed --reason --force` now change behavior/exit.
scenarios: Operator/script passes a value beginning with '-' via the space form, e.g. `--reason -see-below` or `--assignee --team`; old code accepted it as the literal value, new code exits 1 with 'requires a value'.
A following flag intended as the value, e.g. `--assignee --review`, previously bound '--review' as the assignee.
